  • comparison to other samples. This test is useful for testing foods that have an after taste or

questions.question: State the purpose of conducting a monadic test.
questions.solution_html:
• Mention the importance of identifying the problem before conducting a sensory test.
  • Answer: The first factor to be considered by panel leader is to identify the problem to be
  • looked into i.e., aim of the test should be known. Since sensory organs are simulated
  • simultaneously, for example, aroma and taste, colour and appearance, etc, the objective of
  • testing has to be clear and focussed. The judge has to look for these attributes only.

  • evaluation procedure for accurate results.

questions.question: Define Numerical Scoring Test.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: The volatility of aromas is related to the temperature of the food. High temperatures
  • tend to volatilise aromatic compounds, making them quite apparent for Judging; cool or cold
  • temperatures inhibit volatilisation.
  • ❖ Increase in temperature increases aroma volatility.
  • ❖ V olatile compounds evaporate more rapidly at higher temperatures.
  • ❖ Aroma perception becomes stronger with increased release of volatile compounds.
  • ❖ Extremely high temperature may destroy delicate aroma compounds.
  • ❖ Low temperature reduces aroma release and sensory perception.
questions.final_answer: ❖ Low temperature reduces aroma release and sensory perception.
